title: Taifa of Niebla
capsule: The Taifa of Niebla was an Andalusi petty kingdom in the lower Odiel-Tinto basin of southwestern Iberia, centered at Niebla (Huelva province), that maintained independence across three intermittent periods under three successive dynasties: the Yahsubids c. 1023–1053, the Bitruyids c. 1145–1150, and the Mahfuzids c. 1234–1262. Between independent phases, Niebla was subject first to the Taifa of Seville under Abbad II al-Mu'tadid and then to the Almohad empire. The Mahfuzid ruler Ibn Mahfuz finally submitted to Alfonso X of Castile in 1262, extinguishing the taifa.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. The taifa's core territory around Niebla is identifiable from Arabic chronicles and Castilian conquest records; precise extent of control over the Huelva hinterland is uncertain.
